initial.A:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a finished, AAA-quality concept review sheet for the existing Legend of the Five Rings EMPEROR EDITION Godot game. Landscape 16:9, extremely detailed, 3840x2160 if supported. This is a proposed game UI design, not a web dashboard.
Input images: 1 is the APPROVED player placard material/frame/typography reference, preserve that polished aged brass frame and worn black lacquer. 2 is the APPROVED icon-led details panel, copy its restrained bevels, small riveted corners, icon medallions, fine gold rules, spacing and quiet readable black lacquer. 3,4,5 are the original full card scans of Daidoji Kenshi, Asahina Konomi, Asahina Yasutora. Reproduce these actual card faces, proportions, names and artwork faithfully without redesigning/cropping/replacing them with invented cards.
Aesthetic: Japanese war-room tabletop game, dark navy woven mat outside menu, warm black worn lacquer inside menu, aged antique brass frames with subtle Japanese corner ornamentation. Warm ivory Caudex regular serif body text, Caudex bold names, WeatheredQuill-style uppercase rough calligraphic headings, close tracking. Fine controlled metallic highlights, restrained patina, handcrafted game art. Readable and spacious; never plain olive-green rectangles. No modern web pills, neon, chunky Gothic skulls, exaggerated gold filigree, funeral scenery, human remains, Japanese-character icons, permanent death claim, resurrection button or game-action buttons in gallery.
Data constraints: Clan Crane has 3 dead Personalities, 2 died honorably and 1 died dishonorably. This is illustrative state. Kenshi and Yasutora died honorably; Konomi died dishonorably. Fallen gallery is specifically dead Personalities, separate from Removed from the Game, which must NOT be merged or styled as the same pile. Keep all gallery/inspection card faces upright and completely visible for reading, even the dishonorable one. Badges outside the printed face carry historical death status: intact ivory-gold fan + 'Died honorably'; broken dark-carmine fan + 'Died dishonorably'. Distinguish shape and words, not just color. No unverified cause/time/honor-penalty data.
In the in-play comparison only: dishonor rotates the ENTIRE existing printed card through exactly 180 degrees, including art, name, numbers and text; bowing adds the existing 90 degree rotation. At 270 degrees, the portrait face is horizontal, counterclockwise relative to upright. This is a visual state comparison, not four new cards or pile entries. A small readable carmine broken-fan marker may sit outside the scan.
Exact small footer: 'Concept only · Illustrative public state'.
VARIANT A — 'A · FALLEN LEDGER'.
Composition: slim sheet heading at top. Upper 72 percent contains two balanced areas: LEFT 26 percent a large close-up of the approved Crane placard plus its new Fallen entry and a little hover explanation; RIGHT 72 percent a complete proposed 'FALLEN CARDS' window. Lower 23 percent a separate wide, orderly orientation comparison across the navy mat. The main gallery must be large enough for three full portrait card faces in one row, no awkward wasted vertical space.
LEFT: Reproduce the approved blue Crane medallion, 'CRANE', small teal 'YOUR TURN', player name 'Crane', and existing three-stat row: gold fan 11; L5R gold coin 2; hand-of-cards icon 5 / 8. Do not squeeze another stat into this row. Directly beneath the same placard attach an elegant shallow lacquer strip matching its width, with small aged-silver kabuto/helmet at rest icon on left, 'Fallen 3' and small chevron on right. The number is live-looking ivory text, no gold circle around it. Thin leader annotation 'Open the Fallen gallery'. Beneath show one small approved-style lacquer tooltip '3 dead Personalities' then '2 honorable · 1 dishonorable'. It should look like a native component detail, not an extra permanent table panel.
RIGHT GALLERY: matching approved black lacquer/brass framed rectangular window. Heading 'FALLEN CARDS', small X close control upper right. Two wide understated player tabs, 'Crane 3' active with subtle gold edge, 'Lion 2' inactive. Smaller subline '3 dead Personalities'. Three equally sized full card faces in a generous single row: Kenshi, Konomi, Yasutora. Beneath each, their name and clear small icon-led historical status captions as specified. Konomi gets a quiet dark red bottom keyline, not red over the whole face. Gentle top hover highlight on Kenshi. Footer 'Hover to read · Click to inspect' on left, understated lacquer 'Back to table' button on right. No extra confirmation.
BOTTOM: small heading 'ON THE TABLE'. Four equally spaced examples of the same Kenshi scan on navy textile, large enough to recognize the whole face. Exact labels below: 'Honorable', 'Bowed', 'Dishonorable', 'Bowed + dishonorable'. Orientations precisely 0,90,180,270 degrees respectively; allow room so horizontal cases do not overlap vertical ones. Place small fan/broken-fan visual key to clarify the difference between normal bowing and dishonor. Have labels and markers stay upright. Strong visual hierarchy, no explanatory paragraphs.

VARIANT B — 'B · FALLEN INSPECTION'.

Clearly different from A: focus on selection and reading.

This is a compact top-corner entry, not A's footer strip. Beneath show hover tooltip in the approved lacquer style: 'Fallen cards' / '3 dead Personalities' / 'Open gallery'. Show this enlarged enough to be reviewable.
RIGHT 74 percent: large approved-style 'FALLEN CARDS' window. Small X. Clan tabs 'Crane 3' and 'Lion 2'. Below tabs, LEFT half is a compact gallery of the three actual cards: two portrait cards in top row Kenshi, Konomi; Yasutora beneath, all full faces shown, names and status labels outside scans. Selected Konomi has precise dark carmine and antique-brass outline. RIGHT half is a large inspection panel integrated into the same window, subtly separated by a thin gold vertical rule. It shows full upright Konomi scan prominently, then an icon-led lacquer status plate: large sculpted broken-fan medallion (dark carmine, aged metal) beside 'Died dishonorably'; second smaller line 'Asahina Konomi'. A second quiet line 'Crane · Fallen Personality'. Nothing else, no invented history. Selected card face remains upright and undamaged. Inspection prioritizes reading, not more clicks. At bottom of window: 'Select a card to inspect' and 'Back to table'.
BOTTOM: two handsome close-up table vignettes, same actual Kenshi card showing 'Dishonorable · Unbowed' at exactly 180 degrees and 'Dishonorable · Bowed' at exactly 270 degrees. Complete face including print rotates; labels outside stay upright. Small broken-fan status marker clear of the artwork, token rail and navy force ribbon. Beside them a concise note 'Cards turn on the table. Inspections stay upright.' Use large elegant type and measured breathing room. No on-table corpse icon or permanently open gallery.

refinements.A: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the edit target: the A FALLEN LEDGER concept sheet. Images 2–4 are supporting ORIGINAL full card scans Kenshi, Konomi, Yasutora, respectively. Preserve the target's layout, gorgeous aged-brass frames, worn black lacquer, original Crane placard, attached Fallen strip, legible status badges, title, scene and typography. Make these tightly scoped corrections: remove ALL blue spear/number ribbons attached to Kenshi in the big gallery and all four bottom examples, leaving only his unchanged complete printed scan with the printed top-left 3 and top-right 3. The gallery represents dead cards, so no live Force ribbon. In the bottom four orientation examples show the ENTIRE complete rectangular Kenshi scan from image 2 at 0,90,180,270 degrees respectively. If necessary make those bottom scans slightly smaller so every printed edge and all bottom text fit. Keep labels and fan icons upright below them. Preserve full scans in main gallery too; don't truncate their bottom text. Keep the four current labels and the rest of the UI exactly the same. No redesigned cards, no new widgets, no new slogans. Preserve image dimensions.
refinements.B: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the edit target: B FALLEN INSPECTION. Images 2,3,4 are the original FULL card scans Kenshi, Konomi, Yasutora. Preserve the lovely aged-brass frame, black lacquer, compact Fallen badge on placard, larger Konomi inspection with broken-fan medallion, clan tabs, title and overall composition. Correct the cropped card thumbnails. Inside the existing gallery window LEFT of the vertical divider replace the 2-column thumbnails with THREE stacked selectable ROWS. Each row fits a COMPLETE upright original portrait scan at its left, about 82px wide and 115px high at this image size, preserving original card aspect ratio 5:7, no crop of title, illustration, lower text or footer. To each thumbnail's right, put the card name and fan icon + historical status. Row 1 Kenshi 'Died honorably'; row 2 Konomi 'Died dishonorably' with muted red fine selection outline; row 3 Yasutora 'Died honorably'. Keep ALL THREE rows visible; use the full available left browser height. The large right Konomi scan also stays complete, upright and undamaged. At bottom of sheet the two comparison cards currently crop the lower printed rules: replace them with FULL ORIGINAL Kenshi scan, one rotated exactly180 degrees and the other270 degrees. They must show the entire physical rectangular card at correct aspect ratio, shrink to fit instead of cropping. At 180, full vertical card top is at bottom; at270 full card is horizontal with title at left and foot at right. Preserve enough space for the text, labels and upright broken-fan icons; no overlap. Remove the extra decorative slogan at bottom-left ('Familiar. Functional...' / 'Same game...') and remove tagline 'Review the dead. Honor remains.' beneath the title, keeping this area calm and sparse. All other elements remain unchanged. No Force ribbons or new widgets. Preserve image dimensions.

DO NOT just add a black footer below an existing crop. REPLACE the graphic with the whole reference, including all pale parchment below the art, printed traits AND the lower paragraph AND the tiny artist/copyright footer. The card face has approximately 40% pale printed area below its illustration. The whole reference must fit inside a rectangle 5 units wide and 7 units tall. Full card scan is visibly taller than wide.

Five exact corrections in the 1672x941 target:
1. Browser Kenshi near x608,y220: fit FULL reference2 into rectangle x620,y222 WIDTH84 HEIGHT118. The entire white lower printed paragraph and black footer must be visible, not only art/stats/type.
2. Browser Konomi near x608,y362: fit FULL reference3 into x620,y368 WIDTH84 HEIGHT118.
3. Browser Yasutora near x608,y507: fit FULL reference4 into x620,y515 WIDTH84 HEIGHT118.
Keep existing row texts and status icons where they are. Since these inserted scans are now narrower, leave remaining space as black lacquer.
4. Bottom Dishonorable Unbowed graphic: FULL reference2 at 180 degrees in x390,y748 WIDTH95 HEIGHT133. The portrait is tall, not nearly square. The paragraph and copyright strip are now at TOP, above the upside-down person. Existing red icon and surrounding text stay.

Do not crop any of these five scans. Scale down whole photos to fit. Keep the rest pixel-faithful to reference1. No decorative additions. Full pale rules/flavor-text areas absolutely must be present on the five smaller cards.

recommendation: A's attached Fallen counter with B's selected-card inspection. User can choose independently.
ux: Per-player authoritative DeadCount, separate from hand count and Honor.
Fallen holds dead Personalities; Removed from the Game stays separate.
Honorable/dishonorable death has icon and text, not color alone.
Table face composes dishonor rotation with bowing. Inspection and gallery faces stay upright.
Death examples are staged public state, not a record of an actual match.
Native implementation must use full uncropped original scans at their true aspect ratio and live approved fonts. Generated small-card proportions/lettering remain illustrative.
